extracted.intended_audience: judge advocates, convening authorities, military commanders, and members of courts-martial (military legal practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for courts-martial concerning admissibility of prior convictions, permitted punishments, sentence drafting and voting practices, clemency recommendations, and the form and content of the official record of proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charge pleading specificity (homicide vs manslaughter)
rubrics_metrics.description: A specification alleging homicide but not adding 'with malice aforethought,' or in terms to that effect, is pleading of manslaughter only and thus within article 62.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the charging language omits 'malice aforethought' the offense should be treated as manslaughter; precise wording of charges controls classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense to embezzlement for loss without fault
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a defense to a charge under article 62 of the embezzlement defined in section 5490 ... that the funds alleged to have been embezzled were, without fault on the part of the accused, lost in transportation or fraudulently or feloniously abstracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where loss occurred through no fault of the accused (transportation loss or third-party abstraction), that fact may defeat embezzlement charges under article 62.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of previous convictions (Executive order March 30, 1898)
rubrics_metrics.description: Previous convictions 'whatever their number within the prescribed period' are admissible to aid the court in determining the proper measure of punishment; limits of punishment operative only in time of peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previous convictions may be shown to inform sentencing, subject to statutory/ordering limits and differing rules in wartime where courts have broader discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadmissibility of prior convictions from prior enlistments (except certain desertion cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Previous convictions except of desertion on a trial for desertion, not adjudged during the current pending enlistment but incurred during a prior enlistment, are not admissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior convictions must generally be those incurred/ adjudged within the current enlistment to be admissible, with limited exceptions (e.g., certain desertion contexts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-admissibility of civil-court convictions in this procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of a previous conviction by a civil court is not admissible in this procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only convictions recognized as 'previous convictions' under military approval rules are admissible; civil convictions do not qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of disapproved findings/sentences on previous conviction admissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of a previous conviction is not admissible where the findings and sentence were disapproved by the proper reviewing authority; 'previous conviction' means a conviction to which effect has been given by the approval of the sentence by competent authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior trial whose sentence was disapproved does not create an admissible 'previous conviction' — approval by reviewing authority is key.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper proof of previous convictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The proper evidence of a previous conviction is the record of the trial or a duly authenticated copy of the record or of the order of promulgation. Copy of the summary court record should be certified by the post commander or adjutant to be a true copy. The certificate of the company commander is not a legal substitute. The statement of service required by Army Regulations is not evidence of previous convictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authenticated trial records or promulgation orders; informal certificates or service statements are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of approval fixes date of conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: As the date of approval fixes the date of conviction, the date of approval is the date to be considered in the receipt of evidence of previous convictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing whether a prior conviction falls within any prescribed period, use the approval date of the sentence as the conviction date.

rubrics_metrics.name: No presentation of prior convictions after acquittal
rubrics_metrics.description: Held that after an acquittal evidence of previous convictions should not be presented to the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not introduce prior convictions once the accused has been acquitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courts may impose punishments sanctioned by custom even if not listed in regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: In a case where its sentence is discretionary, a court-martial may impose any punishment that is sanctioned by custom of the service, although the same may not be included in the list of the more usual punishments contained in the Army Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customary service punishments may be adjudged where sentence is discretionary, subject to law and principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order prescribing maximum punishments and substitutions
rubrics_metrics.description: The order prescribing maximum punishments also provides for certain substitutions of punishment. The purpose ... is not only to determine the measure but also the kind of punishment ... where the prescribed limit is forfeiture and confinement, a reprimand in lieu thereof cannot legally be adjudged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an order prescribes a limit (e.g., forfeiture plus confinement), courts must observe that prescribed kinds/substitutions are authoritative; cannot substitute an inappropriate lesser form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orders may recommend but cannot compel a specific sentence form
rubrics_metrics.description: While a specific punishment may be recommended in orders to be adjudged by courts-martial ... it is not competent to order such courts to adopt a particular form of sentence in any case. The duty and discretion of courts-martial in the imposition of punishments are prescribed and defined by the Articles of War.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanding orders may recommend punishments but cannot remove court discretion to select sentence form within Articles of War.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure punishment by military discipline gravity, not civil criminality
rubrics_metrics.description: The punishment to be imposed by the court-martial should never-theless be measured less by the criminality of the act as a civil offense than by its gravity as a breach of military discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When civil and military proceedings both exist, sentencing by court-martial should focus on injury to military discipline rather than equivalence to civil penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drunkenness on duty (outside maximum-prescribed list) punishable at court discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Drunkenness on duty on occasions other than those specified in the order prescribing maximum punishments are offenses under the thirty-eighth article, for which maximum punishments have not been prescribed. They remain, therefore, punishable at the discretion of the court-martial as authorized by the Articles of War and the custom of the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an offense lacks a statutory maximum, the court has sentencing discretion within Articles of War and custom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local/foreign laws not always determinative for territorial offenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision that punishment 'shall not be less than the punishment provided for the like offense by the laws of the State, Territory or district in which such offense may have been committed' did not refer to local laws of Porto Rico at that time or to foreign governments; a court can properly fix such punishment as may seem adequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where local law is foreign or inapplicable, the court may set punishment adequate to the offense rather than strictly conform to unfamiliar local penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended practice for arriving at a sentence (writing and voting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Best approved practice: for each member to write a sentence and deposit it with the judge advocate; and (no sentence having been adopted by a majority of votes) for the court, after all sentences have been read to it by the judge advocate, to proceed to vote upon them in the order of their severity, beginning with the least severe, until some one of those proposed is agreed upon by a majority of votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This stepwise, written-and-vote procedure is recommended though not mandatory; courts may adopt other methods in their discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to vote on punishment after conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: After a conviction each member of the court should vote for a punishment appropriate to the offense ... without regard to whether or not he believes the accused innocent or guilty. A refusal by a member to vote a punishment after a conviction is a neglect of duty under the sixty-second article of war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members must participate in punishment voting; abstention where convicted is dereliction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid variances between finding/sentence and charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Care should be taken that there be no variance in the statement of the name, etc., of the accused, between the finding or sentence and the charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistency of identity and procedural particulars across charges, findings, and sentences to avoid irregularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprimand execution should be directed to convening commander
rubrics_metrics.description: A court-martial, in imposing the punishment of reprimand, will, if adding anything in regard to its execution, properly direct that the reprimand be administered by the commander who convened the court. A sentence to be reprimanded by an officer inferior to the convening authority is not in accordance with the approved practice of the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sentencing specifies administration of reprimand, do so by the convening authority; otherwise leave execution details to reviewing officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay forfeiture must be expressly adjudged
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay cannot be forfeited (in a sentence) by implication. If the court intends to forfeit pay, the penalty of forfeiture should be adjudged in express terms in the sentence. No other punishment ... involves per se a forfeiture or deprivation of any part of the pay or allowances due the party at the time of the approval or taking effect of the sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To affect pay, the sentence must expressly state the forfeiture; other listed punishments do not automatically forfeit pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture amount must be clearly fixed in the sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: A court-martial, in forfeiting pay by sentence, should so fix the amount to be forfeited that the same will clearly and unmistakably appear from the sentence itself without a reference to any order or other source of information being necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentences that tie forfeiture amount to an outside valuation (e.g., 'value of property') without specifying amount are irregular and may be disapproved unless corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot forfeit special-bailment local bounty
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a soldier on enlisting was paid an amount as local bounty and this money was held by authorities as a special bailment and trust for his benefit, the court was not authorized to forfeit this money by its sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts should not forfeit funds that are private property held in trust by authorities rather than pay due from the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fining for government witness attendance costs not proper punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Imposing a fine equal to the estimated cost to the Government of procuring attendance of witnesses (based on affidavit that witnesses expected to show material matters but did not) was held not a proper basis for such fine as punishment; conduct, if culpable, should be charged separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the sentencing power to fine a convicted party for matters that should be separately charged and tried.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court cannot direct transfer when reducing NCO to ranks
rubrics_metrics.description: A court-martial, in sentencing a noncommissioned officer to be reduced to the ranks, is not empowered to direct that when reduced he be transferred to another regiment or company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers fall under separate authority; sentence reductions should not attempt to direct transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loss of files/steps is a recognized punishment for commissioned officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Loss of, or reduction in, files or steps (relative rank) in the list of the officers of his grade, is a recognized legal punishment by sentence of court-martial in a case of a commissioned officer; it is a continuing punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduction in seniority can be used as continuing punishment but has unequal effects; courts should be mindful of its impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension (form and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: The punishment of suspension, as imposed by sentence, is usually in the form of a suspension from rank or from command for a stated term, sometimes accompanied by suspension from pay for the same period. Suspension from rank includes suspension from command. Suspension takes effect upon notice of the approval of the sentence officially communicated to the officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court should specify form and term; effect begins on official notification or promulgation; suspension does not per se create confinement status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confinement during suspension is permissive, not inherent
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension from rank does not involve a status of confinement or arrest. In sentencing an officer to be suspended from rank, it is not unusual for the court to require that he be confined during the term of suspension to his proper station ... Where this is not done, the suspended officer is not entitled to leave, though leaves of absence are frequently granted under such circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If confinement is desired during suspension, the sentence should state it; otherwise suspension differs from confinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place of confinement phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: In imposing a sentence of confinement at a military prison, the court should properly add 'at such place as the proper authority may designate,' or words to that effect. To direct that the place be designated by an officer inferior to the convening authority is irregular and improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentence should leave designation of confinement place to proper authority, not an inferior officer named in the sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imprisonment may extend beyond enlistment term and remain legal
rubrics_metrics.description: A general court-martial is authorized to adjudge a term of imprisonment to extend beyond the end of the pending term of enlistment of the soldier ... such sentences may be executed with the same legality as any other sentence of imprisonment; upon determination of the enlistment the party continues to be held under sentence as a civilian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may sentence beyond enlistment; execution continues even after enlistment ends, subject to promulgation and discharge timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentences of confinement until fine paid and maximum limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentences of imprisonment till a fine, also imposed by the sentence, are sanctioned by the usage of the service. It is proper in such sentences to affix a limit beyond which the confinement shall not be continued in any event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When tying imprisonment to payment of a fine, the sentence should set an absolute maximum confinement period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-trial confinement considered in sentencing
rubrics_metrics.description: The fact that the accused has been confined for an unreasonable period awaiting trial may properly be taken into consideration by the court in estimating the period of confinement to be imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts should account for any excessive pre-trial detention when determining confinement lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ball and chain and other corporal/ornamental punishments should be rare
rubrics_metrics.description: The punishment of ball and chain, though sanctioned by usage, should be imposed only in extreme cases. Its remission has generally been recommended except in cases of old offenders or aggravated crimes. Such penalties (and shaking the head, drumming out) have become rare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise restraint; prefer remission except in severe or repeat-offender cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal mandatory for certain officer offenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts-martial are required to adjudge dismissal upon officers of the Army by specified articles of war upon conviction of the specific offenses therein described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For enumerated articles, the sentencing duty is mandatory (e.g., dismissal/cashiering) and courts must follow statutory prescription.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military duty as punishment is degrading and should be disapproved
rubrics_metrics.description: Military duty is honorable, and to impose it in any form as a punishment must tend to degrade it ... sentences imposing 'guard duty' for certain periods should properly be disapproved. So held regarding sentences requiring a deserter to serve for an additional year after expiration of term as punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sentencing that degrades military duty by converting ordinary duties into punishment; such sentences are improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court cannot legally extend enlistment/service term as punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: A sentence cannot legally extend the time of the service of a soldier as such beyond the term for which he originally contracted. Thus a court has no power to prolong enlistment by adding an additional period by way of punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentences must not attempt to lengthen contracted service terms; remedies for 'making good' lost time arise from contractual liability, not court punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court cannot sentence soldier to deposit part of his pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Held that a court-martial can not legally sentence a soldier to deposit any part of his pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentences should not require depositing pay; pay-related commands must conform to rules on forfeiture and explicit adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court may animadvert upon other officers' conduct in proper cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The remarking by the court, in connection with the finding or sentence, unfavorably upon an officer or soldier (other than the accused) whose conduct is exhibited by the testimony ... is sanctioned by the authorities as permissible and regular in a proper case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may note adverse observations about third parties based on the record, but should exercise caution and propriety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animadversion upon witnesses permitted but to be used cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: A court-martial may, in connection with its judgment, properly animadvert upon a witness not only as testifying falsely, but as giving evasive and disingenuous testimony; but the power to thus animadvert upon witnesses should be exercised with caution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticizing witness credibility is allowable but must be measured and sparing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation of clemency is not part of official record
rubrics_metrics.description: A recommendation of the accused to clemency is no part of the official record of the trial ... but is merely the personal act of the members who sign it. It should not therefore be incorporated with the record proper, but should be appended to or transmitted with the same as a separate and independent paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clemency recommendations should be separate documents appended to the record, not integrated into the formal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Members should refrain from weak/ill-considered clemency recommendations; state specific grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Members will, in general, do well to refrain from subscribing recommendations where the testimony ... fails clearly to justify a remission or mitigation. Members should be careful to state the specific grounds upon which they base the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid perfunctory clemency recommendations; provide explicit grounds to allow reviewing authority to assess merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple separate clemency recommendations allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of a court-martial desiring to recommend an accused to clemency need not all sign the same statement. There may be, in any case, two or more separate recommendations each signed by different members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may transmit multiple, separately-signed clemency statements rather than a single unified recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of appended recommendation is exceptional; better to file explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where members who had joined in a recommendation applied to have the same withdrawn on the ground that their opinions had changed, such a proceeding would be exceptional and irregular; preferable course is to file with the record the application and statement of the members so that the same might be referred to and considered in connection with the recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to withdraw an already appended recommendation; submit a supplemental explanatory statement instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections to sentence meaning require reconvening the court
rubrics_metrics.description: Where, after a sentence had been adjudged, the majority transmitted a written statement that the sentence was intended to have a certain meaning not conveyed by its terms, held that such irregular statement could have no effect as a correction of the sentence; the proposed correction could only be made by the court itself after having been reconvened to reconsider the sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive corrections to sentence wording/meaning must be made by the court reconvened, not by post-hoc statements to reviewing authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court-martial record should be a full report including all testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: It is contemplated by statute that a court-martial shall make a formal record of its proceedings ... the record of a court-martial has come to be, in our practice, a full report and recital of the details of the trial in each case, including all the testimony introduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a comprehensive record covering proceedings and testimony to inform reviewing authority; follow Army Regulations and Court-Martial Manual directions on form and substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practice: include irregular proceedings and note excluded documents
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the better practice that all the proceedings—even those that are irregular—which transpire in connection with a trial or at a revision should be set out in the record ... It is, however, not necessary to encumber a record by spreading upon it documents excluded by the court. But the character of the writing and the grounds upon which it was ruled out should be specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document irregular events and reasons for excluding material so reviewing authorities understand context without reproducing excluded documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convene order copy and completeness in record
rubrics_metrics.description: The copy of the convening order ... should properly be prefixed to the proceedings, as constituting the initial authority for the existence and action of the court. This order should of course be complete, and should exhibit ... that it has proceeded from a commanding officer competent to order the court. Where several cases are tried by the same court, a separate copy of the order should be incorporated in the record in each case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each case record must include a complete convening order showing authority and any subsequent modifying orders to establish lawful composition and jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record must show authority under which each member acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Held that the record of proceedings of a general court-martial should show the authority under which each member of the court acts as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detail in record proving each member's lawful appointment to the court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record must show organization, quorum, members present, and accused's attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: The record should show that the court met and organized pursuant to the order ... there should assemble at least a quorum, i.e., five ... The record of the first assembling should specify the members present by name, rank, etc. The record should also show the presence of the accused at the time of the organization and at all material stages and portions of the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document initial organization (names/ranks), quorum, daily attendance of members, and accused's presence at material stages to ensure procedural regularity.
